title: Reading and writing a move (part 3 of 3)
outcomes: Names the piece, the squares and any capture, check or castling in a written move
Plays an eight-move score on the board, from either colour and on a turned board
Adds a file letter (or a rank number when both pieces share a file) when two pieces of the same kind can make the move
Knows that marks such as ! and ? do not change the move
Reads and writes promotion (=Q) and long and short castling records
sources: Standard algebraic notation: the FIDE Laws of Chess, Appendix C [R], not re-read in this session
Descriptive notation of older books [R]; the aloud-reading idea is [H], untested here
docs/lesson-depth-standard.md (class A); docs/competition-chess-steps.md (short explanation, many exercises)

steps.text: Part 3 of 3: Reading and writing a move. This part covers Check yourself. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

**Say it back.** A record names the piece (a capital letter, none for a pawn) and the square where it lands. Add x for a capture, + for check, # for mate, O-O or O-O-O for castling, and =Q for a new queen. If two pieces of one kind could go to the square, add the file, or the rank when the file is shared. The marks ! and ? never change the move.

steps.prompt: Teach it back. In your own words, tell a friend how to write two knights on b1 and f3 both going to d2, and why the b matters. Did you mention the letter, x, + or #, and the extra file or rank?

steps.caption: Look again, from an earlier part of this lesson. A score that begins with a Black move. The dots show whose turn it is.

line.say: 1...d5: three dots, because this score starts with Black's move. A pawn, so no letter.
2.c4: White attacks the pawn on d5 with a pawn.
2...e6: a pawn move, no letter. It defends d5 and opens a path for the bishop [I].
3.Nc3: N is the knight. Now two white pieces attack d5.
3...Nf6: Black's knight comes out and adds another defender of d5, three in all.
4.Bg5: the bishop comes out and attacks the knight on f6.
4...Be7: Black's bishop steps out; the knight on f6 stays defended.
5.e3: a pawn move, no letter. It opens the diagonal of White's bishop on f1.

claims.statement: After Bg5 the bishop attacks the knight on f6.
After Nc3 two white pieces attack d5.
After Nf6 three black pieces defend d5.
After Be7 the knight on f6 is defended twice.
The bishop still stands on f1.

steps.text: **Remember.** A record names the piece and the square where it lands, with x for a capture, + for check and # for mate. Ask yourself: could another piece of the same kind go there too? If so, add the file, or the rank when the file is shared. The marks ! and ? never change the move.
